verification.note: Reproduced by reading the code. In frontend/src/app/drive/[name]/page.tsx, lines 19-35 branch only on trash, missing, inbox and home. Lines 37-38 send any other non-null view to `<FolderBrowser view={view} .../>` without a folderPath, and the page never names `continue`. normaliseDriveView (frontend/src/lib/driveViews.ts:35-37) rewrites only `library`, so `continue` reaches FolderBrowser unchanged. The new row at page.test.tsx:65 therefore passes the checks at :99-103 (component is FolderBrowser) and :105-111 (folderPath undefined, view === 'continue') for any string at all; :145-161 already gets the same result for 'not-a-view'. The name check at :83-97 only covers branched views, and it filters out FolderBrowser rows. The only thing the row changes is that the length assertion at :96 goes to 10. Taking `continue` out of CROSS_FOLDER_VIEWS (driveViews.ts:9) or out of useFolderFiles would not fail this file. The commit's stated aim, covering the continue view in the route table, is therefore not something this test can check.

specification_compliance: I10 (`?view=continue` requests filter=continue with limit=50): this commit's page.test.tsx does not check it. The route only passes the view through, and the wiring that matters lives in useFolderFiles/driveViews, which this test file does not cover.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Unknown `?view=` values go to the drive-wide FolderBrowser listing on purpose (page.test.tsx:143-161), so a typo in a view name gives a working-looking screen rather than an error.
regression_risks: If `continue` were dropped from CROSS_FOLDER_VIEWS or from the view-to-filter mapping, the route tests would stay green.
test_coverage: page.test.tsx:65 adds a `continue` row that cannot tell a wired view from an unknown one; it adds no discriminating coverage.
The real check for the continue view has to come from useFolderFiles, driveViews, layout, sidebar or page-jump tests, which were not inspected here.
